chunks: The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) informed me, from Abu Ja'far ibn Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn Ja'far,

He said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about building upon a grave and sitting upon it — is it permissible? He said: It is not permissible to build upon it, nor to sit [upon it], nor to plaster it with gypsum, nor to coat it with clay.

key_terms.الْبِنَاءُ: construction — erecting any permanent structure on a grave
key_terms.تَجْصِيصُهُ: plastering with gypsum (jass) — applying white lime plaster to the grave surface
key_terms.تَطْيِينُهُ: coating with clay/mud — smearing the grave with mud or clay
key_terms.يَصْلُحُ: is it proper/permissible — a classical fiqh formula querying the licitness of an action

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) rule regarding building on graves and plastering them with gypsum or clay?
ai.summary: Ali ibn Ja'far — the brother of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) — directly questions the Imam about four grave-related practices. The Imam issues a fourfold prohibition: erecting a structure, sitting on the grave, applying a gypsum plaster (tajsis), and smearing it with clay (tatyin). This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh on the proper treatment of graves, found in Chapter 128 of al-Istibsar.
